lessons.title: Begin and end an exchange
lessons.outcome: I can greet someone and take leave.

lessons.title: Exchange names
lessons.outcome: I can ask and give a name with a model.

lessons.title: Ask a name politely
lessons.outcome: I can choose a polite name question for a stranger.

lessons.title: Thank and ask politely
lessons.outcome: I can use grazie, prego, scusi and per favore in their different jobs.

lessons.title: Ask for a repeat
lessons.outcome: I can say I do not understand and ask for repetition.

lessons.title: Say where you are from
lessons.outcome: I can use Sono di with a supplied place name.

lessons.title: Read two c patterns
lessons.outcome: I can connect familiar c spellings with their taught sounds.

lessons.title: Keep c hard before e and i
lessons.outcome: I can recognize ch in a few introduced words.

lessons.title: Complete a first supported exchange
lessons.outcome: I can greet a peer, give a name and origin, ask for repetition and close the exchange.

formModels.description: An introduction gives your own name with mi chiamo and origin with sono di. E tu? gives the other person a turn. Piacere is a friendly meeting phrase, not a name or a place.

When you miss a message, ask for a repeat rather than guessing a name. Può ripetere, per favore? is a taught polite chunk. At the end, arrivederci is a polite goodbye; a domani is appropriate when you expect to meet tomorrow.

lessons.title: Use sono, sei and è
lessons.outcome: I can choose essere for I, familiar you, and one other person.

lessons.title: Use Lei è politely
lessons.outcome: I can ask or tell who a person is using polite Lei.

lessons.title: Introduce two or more people
lessons.outcome: I can use siamo, siete and sono with plural people.

lessons.title: Give vowels and stress their place
lessons.outcome: I can recognize familiar vowel spellings and marked final stress.

lessons.title: Keep the written accent
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish e from è and preserve familiar final accents.

lessons.title: Name a familiar noun
lessons.outcome: I can use il or la with familiar singular nouns.

lessons.title: Introduce one thing
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish un, una and un’ with a familiar noun.

lessons.title: Name a student or a backpack
lessons.outcome: I can use lo/uno and l’ with their taught nouns.

lessons.title: Say what one person has
lessons.outcome: I can use ho, hai and ha for possessions.

lessons.title: Say what a group has
lessons.outcome: I can choose abbiamo, avete and hanno.

lessons.title: Read small numbers
lessons.outcome: I can recognize and say zero through ten in practical information.

lessons.title: Give an age and a need
lessons.outcome: I can use avere to state a modeled age or hunger and thirst.

lessons.title: Write h without sounding it
lessons.outcome: I can keep the silent h in familiar avere forms.

lessons.title: Make familiar nouns plural
lessons.outcome: I can form regular plurals of taught nouns.

lessons.title: Put an article before a plural
lessons.outcome: I can choose i, gli and le for taught plurals.

lessons.title: Keep a hard sound in the plural
lessons.outcome: I can write amiche and know that città does not change.

lessons.title: Match a basic description
lessons.outcome: I can match piccolo or grande to a familiar noun.

lessons.title: Give double consonants time
lessons.outcome: I can preserve a familiar single/double-consonant spelling contrast.

lessons.title: Say who speaks or lives somewhere
lessons.outcome: I can use regular -are verbs with I, you, and one other person.

lessons.title: Talk about a group action
lessons.outcome: I can use -iamo, -ate and -ano for regular -are verbs.

lessons.title: Ask a simple question
lessons.outcome: I can ask a yes/no or dove question using a taught present form.

lessons.title: Say what does not happen
lessons.outcome: I can put non before a known present verb.

lessons.title: Turn a statement into a question
lessons.outcome: I can recognize a familiar question and practise its intonation.

lessons.title: Use vivere and prendere
lessons.outcome: I can choose present -ere forms for familiar persons.

lessons.title: Use dormire and partire
lessons.outcome: I can use ordinary -ire endings with a known verb.

lessons.title: Use capire
lessons.outcome: I can use the taught -isc- forms of capire.

lessons.title: Read g and gh in familiar words
lessons.outcome: I can recognize the taught hard and soft g patterns.

lessons.title: Say where you go
lessons.outcome: I can use selected present forms of andare in a plan.

lessons.title: Say what you do or make
lessons.outcome: I can use selected forms of fare in familiar activities.

lessons.title: Say who comes
lessons.outcome: I can use selected present forms of venire.

lessons.title: Go to a city or country
lessons.outcome: I can use a with taught cities and in with taught countries.

lessons.title: Come from and go with
lessons.outcome: I can use da for source and con for a companion.

lessons.title: Read sc and sch
lessons.outcome: I can recognize the taught soft sc and hard sc/sch patterns.

lessons.title: Say what is there
lessons.outcome: I can choose c’è or ci sono for one or several things.

lessons.title: Say where a place is
lessons.outcome: I can say a familiar thing is near or far from a known place.

lessons.title: Join a or in to an article
lessons.outcome: I can use al/alla and nel/nella with familiar places.

lessons.title: Say something is mine
lessons.outcome: I can match mio/mia/miei/mie to a known noun.

lessons.title: Talk about your family
lessons.outcome: I can say mia madre and tuo padre without an article.

lessons.title: Point to this or that
lessons.outcome: I can select questo/questa and quel/quella for familiar things.

lessons.title: Read gn and gli as groups
lessons.outcome: I can recognize gn and gli in introduced everyday words.

lessons.title: Recognize eleven through twenty
lessons.outcome: I can read and use selected numbers from eleven to twenty.

lessons.title: Ask and understand a price
lessons.outcome: I can use introduced tens in a simple euro price.

lessons.title: Make a simple appointment
lessons.outcome: I can use a taught day and alle/all’una with a clock time.

lessons.title: Say many or few
lessons.outcome: I can match molto/poco to familiar count and mass nouns.

lessons.title: Ask if you can do something
lessons.outcome: I can use posso, puoi and polite può before an infinitive.

lessons.title: Say what you want or need to do
lessons.outcome: I can choose taught present forms of volere and dovere before a known infinitive.

lessons.title: Say what you like
lessons.outcome: I can choose mi piace or mi piacciono for a known thing.

lessons.title: Ask a familiar person to act
lessons.outcome: I can use a taught tu command and its negative.

lessons.title: Join a simple reason
lessons.outcome: I can distinguish e, ma and perché in a short statement.

lessons.title: Say what you did yesterday
lessons.outcome: I can use avere plus a regular -ato participle for a completed act.

lessons.title: Finish another kind of verb
lessons.outcome: I can use the taught -uto and -ito participles with avere.

lessons.title: Say you went or arrived
lessons.outcome: I can use selected essere past forms with stated subject agreement.

lessons.title: Send a short note about yesterday
lessons.outcome: I can choose a taught completed form in a simple message.

lessons.title: Use a short written message
lessons.outcome: I can find a practical detail in a short written message.

lessons.title: Understand a short spoken exchange
lessons.outcome: I can pick out a practical detail from a short recording.

lessons.title: Ask who, what, where and when
lessons.outcome: I can open a question with chi, che cosa, dove or quando and put the verb next.

lessons.title: Ask how, why, how many and which
lessons.outcome: I can ask with come, perché, quanto and quale, and make quanto and quale agree with the noun.

lessons.title: Match a question to its answer
lessons.outcome: I can give the kind of answer a question word asks for and use perché both for why and for because.

lessons.title: Join a to every article
lessons.outcome: I can choose al, allo, all’, alla, ai, agli or alle from the noun’s article, and say clock times.

lessons.title: Join di to every article
lessons.outcome: I can choose del, dello, dell’, della, dei, degli or delle to say whose something is or where it comes from.

lessons.unitTitle: Describe a home and its people
lessons.title: Find things in a home
lessons.outcome: I can say which room an object is in and describe a small home.

formModels.description: In cucina means in the kitchen; in bagno means in the bathroom. Nella camera means in the bedroom. Say where the named object is, rather than how many there are.
Su + il becomes sul: sul tavolo, on the table. Learn accanto al letto as a useful location phrase: next to the bed.

lessons.unitTitle: Describe a home and its people
lessons.title: Introduce your family
lessons.outcome: I can introduce relatives and distinguish their relationship, name and age.

formModels.description: Mio fratello and mia sorella normally have no article when the family noun is singular and unmodified. Plural i miei genitori keeps the article.
A person is identified with essere, but age uses avere + number + anni. Do not change the person when changing the number.

editorial.author: Parola curriculum workstream
editorial.textOrigin: Original authored teaching and fictional situations; no third-party text copied.

lessons.title: Say when you get up
lessons.outcome: I can use a few explained reflexive actions in a daily routine.

formModels.description: For these reflexive actions, mi belongs with io, ti with tu, si with lui/lei or polite Lei. Alzarsi: mi alzo, ti alzi, si alza. Lavarsi: mi lavo, ti lavi, si lava. The small word belongs before the conjugated verb.
Alzarsi: noi ci alziamo, voi vi alzate, loro si alzano. Lavarsi: noi ci laviamo, voi vi lavate, loro si lavano. Loro uses si like a singular person, but the verb has the plural ending.

editorial.author: Parola curriculum workstream
editorial.textOrigin: Original authored teaching and fictional situations; no third-party text copied.

lessons.title: Describe work and study
lessons.outcome: I can describe a simple work or study routine and ask about someone else’s.

formModels.description: Lavorare uses lavoro, lavori, lavora, lavoriamo, lavorate, lavorano; polite Lei lavora. Studiare uses studio, studi, studia, studiamo, studiate, studiano; polite Lei studia. Use in ufficio for at the office and in biblioteca for at the library.
Finire adds -isc- in finisco, finisci, finisce and finiscono. Noi finiamo and voi finite have no -isc-. Polite Lei finisce. The time follows alle for these hours.

editorial.author: Parola curriculum workstream
editorial.textOrigin: Original authored teaching and fictional situations; no third-party text copied.

lessons.title: Order and check the bill
lessons.outcome: I can order a familiar item politely and ask its price.

introducedSenses.en: I would like · a polite request chunk

formModels.description: Use vorrei as a polite request chunk: vorrei un tè. You can also make a short noun request with per favore. Un panino is one sandwich; due panini is two.
Quanto costa? asks the price of one thing. Quanto costano? asks about several. Here the item, rather than a person, is the subject: un panino costa, due panini costano.

editorial.author: Parola curriculum workstream
editorial.textOrigin: Original authored teaching and fictional situations; no third-party text copied.

lessons.title: Choose what you prefer
lessons.outcome: I can express a drink preference and distinguish liking one thing from several.

formModels.description: Preferire uses preferisco, preferisci, preferisce, preferiamo, preferite, preferiscono; polite Lei preferisce. Preferisco il tè says what I prefer. The question Tè o caffè? offers alternatives with o.
In mi piace, the thing liked controls the verb. A singular noun or an activity takes piace. Several countable things take piacciono. Pasta and frutta are singular food nouns here.

editorial.author: Parola curriculum workstream
editorial.textOrigin: Original authored teaching and fictional situations; no third-party text copied.

lessons.title: Describe the clothes you wear
lessons.outcome: I can name familiar clothes and match their colours.

introducedSenses.en: to wear; to put on clothing

formModels.description: Rosso changes to rossa, rossi, rosse; nero changes to nera, neri, nere; bianco changes to bianca, bianchi, bianche. Blu is unchanged. The colour agrees with the clothes, regardless of who wears them.
Indossare uses indosso, indossi, indossa, indossiamo, indossate, indossano; polite Lei indossa. It can describe the clothing someone is wearing.

editorial.author: Parola curriculum workstream
editorial.textOrigin: Original authored teaching and fictional situations; no third-party text copied.

lessons.title: Ask for a size in a shop
lessons.outcome: I can ask for a clothing size and permission to try an item.

introducedSenses.en: it is fine; it fits the purpose

formModels.description: For a simple shop request, keep taglia piccola, taglia media or taglia grande together. These adjectives describe the feminine word taglia. Vorrei una taglia media is a polite request.

Posso provare questa giacca? asks permission to try the jacket on. Posso is the speaker’s form of potere; provare stays in the infinitive. Può aiutarmi? is a separate polite help chunk meaning Can you help me?

editorial.author: Parola curriculum workstream
editorial.textOrigin: Original authored teaching and fictional situations; no third-party text copied.

lessons.title: Say what the weather is like
lessons.outcome: I can describe familiar weather and distinguish weather from personal comfort.

formModels.description: Che tempo fa? asks about the weather. Use the fixed weather expressions fa caldo, fa freddo, piove, c’è il sole and c’è vento. Weather fa stays singular; it has no personal subject here.

Use avere for personal comfort: ho caldo/freddo, hai caldo/freddo, ha caldo/freddo, abbiamo caldo/freddo, avete caldo/freddo, hanno caldo/freddo. Polite Lei ha caldo/freddo. Caldo and freddo stay unchanged in these expressions.

editorial.author: Parola curriculum workstream
editorial.textOrigin: Original authored teaching and fictional situations; no third-party text copied.

lessons.title: Choose a plan for the weather
lessons.outcome: I can give a simple weather reason and choose between going out and staying home.

formModels.description: Uscire uses esco, esci, esce, usciamo, uscite, escono; polite Lei esce. Restare uses resto, resti, resta, restiamo, restate, restano; polite Lei resta. Say resto a casa for staying home.
Perché connects an action to its reason. Ma connects a contrast. A rainy day can be a reason to stay home, but someone can choose to go out despite it; follow the meaning supplied by the task.

editorial.author: Parola curriculum workstream
editorial.textOrigin: Original authored teaching and fictional situations; no third-party text copied.

lessons.title: Say how you feel
lessons.outcome: I can state a simple symptom and distinguish a feeling from weather.

introducedSenses.en: to be; to feel in these expressions

formModels.description: Stare uses sto, stai, sta, stiamo, state, stanno; polite Lei sta. Bene and male stay unchanged. Ask Come stai? of a friend and Come sta? of someone addressed politely.
Use avere in ho la febbre and ho mal di testa. Use essere with stanco/stanca: sono stanco for a male speaker, sono stanca for a female speaker. The symptoms do not change the person of avere.

editorial.author: Parola curriculum workstream
editorial.textOrigin: Original authored teaching and fictional situations; no third-party text copied.

lessons.title: Ask for help and an appointment
lessons.outcome: I can ask where a pharmacy is and request a medical appointment as a taught service exchange.

formModels.description: Ho bisogno di + noun says what you need. Keep ho bisogno di un medico as a useful chunk for now. Dov’è la farmacia? asks for a place; può aiutarmi? asks a person politely for help.
Vorrei un appuntamento asks politely for an appointment. Oggi o domani? offers two days. Alle dieci means at ten. Confirm the time you heard, rather than repeating a different time.

editorial.author: Parola curriculum workstream
editorial.textOrigin: Original authored teaching and fictional situations; no third-party text copied.

lessons.title: Say a calendar date
lessons.outcome: I can give a day and month and distinguish the first day from other dates.

formModels.description: Dates use il + day + month: il cinque maggio. The first day uses primo: il primo maggio. Twenty-one is ventuno and twenty-eight is ventotto: the final i of venti disappears before uno or otto. Thirty-one is trentuno.

Italian month names are normally written with a lower-case initial. Gennaio is January, marzo March, maggio May, luglio July, ottobre October and dicembre December. Keep the day and month as separate details.

editorial.author: Parola curriculum workstream
editorial.textOrigin: Original authored teaching and fictional situations; no third-party text copied.

lessons.title: Check when a place opens
lessons.outcome: I can ask about opening and closing times and distinguish now from a regular time.

formModels.description: Aprire uses apro, apri, apre, apriamo, aprite, aprono. Chiudere uses chiudo, chiudi, chiude, chiudiamo, chiudete, chiudono. Polite Lei apre/chiude. A che ora apre? asks when a place opens.
È aperto describes a present state; apre alle nove gives the opening time. Aperto/chiuso agree with the place: la farmacia è aperta, i negozi sono chiusi. Dalle nove alle sei gives a time range.

editorial.author: Parola curriculum workstream
editorial.textOrigin: Original authored teaching and fictional situations; no third-party text copied.

lessons.title: Find a date in a calendar
lessons.outcome: I can recover a date from a familiar calendar and recognise all twelve month names.

lessons.title: Understand a short route
lessons.outcome: I can ask for a familiar destination and distinguish left, right and straight ahead.

formModels.description: A destra means right; a sinistra means left; dritto means straight ahead. Gira a destra is a familiar instruction. Giri a destra and vada dritto are polite instructions to one person, taught as route chunks here.

Scusi, dov’è la stazione? starts a polite location request. Confirm A destra? or A sinistra? when checking a turn. The route can then be repeated. Use gira to a friend, and giri in this polite exchange.

editorial.author: Parola curriculum workstream
editorial.textOrigin: Original authored teaching and fictional situations; no third-party text copied.

lessons.title: Arrange where to meet
lessons.outcome: I can propose a place and time and confirm a meeting arrangement.

introducedSenses.en: we’ll see each other; let’s meet · a chunk

formModels.description: Ci vediamo is a familiar arrangement chunk. Add the place and time. Davanti alla stazione means in front of the station; al bar means at the café.
Va bene accepts an arrangement. Non posso says you cannot; it is not confirmation. After a changed proposal, repeat the new time so both speakers agree.

editorial.author: Parola curriculum workstream
editorial.textOrigin: Original authored teaching and fictional situations; no third-party text copied.

lessons.title: Invite someone to a simple activity
lessons.outcome: I can invite a friend and give a short acceptance or refusal.

formModels.description: Ascoltare uses ascolto, ascolti, ascolta, ascoltiamo, ascoltate, ascoltano; polite Lei ascolta. Leggere uses leggo, leggi, legge, leggiamo, leggete, leggono; polite Lei legge. Ascolto la musica and leggo un libro say what you do.

Vuoi venire al cinema stasera? asks a friend whether they want to come. Sì, volentieri accepts warmly. Mi dispiace, non posso declines politely. A refusal does not mean the invitation was misunderstood.

editorial.author: Parola curriculum workstream
editorial.textOrigin: Original authored teaching and fictional situations; no third-party text copied.

lessons.title: Ask for a contact detail
lessons.outcome: I can request and confirm a name or telephone number without changing its meaning.

introducedSenses.en: How is it spelled? · a chunk

introducedSenses.it: Qual è il suo numero di telefono?

formModels.description: Qual è il suo numero di telefono? asks a person politely for their telephone number. Qual è has no apostrophe. Come si scrive? asks how a name is spelled; Può ripetere lentamente? asks for a slower repeat. These are useful whole questions at this stage.

A confirmation preserves the sequence of digits or the supplied name. Zero sei nove is 069, not 096. Ask for a repeat when unsure; do not substitute a familiar number. The short digit strings here are fictional practice, not real contact numbers.

lessons.title: Read and relay a practical note
lessons.outcome: I can find and pass on the day, time or place in short familiar notices.

lessons.title: Follow a changed arrangement
lessons.outcome: I can recover the final detail from a clearly spoken familiar service or meeting exchange.
